headlines.title: 5 Dividend Stocks That Have Raised Payouts for Decades. Are They Still Buys?
headlines.summary: A decades-long raise streak can hide a thin cushion underneath. Five dividend veterans face the same test: does today's cash flow fund tomorrow's raise? One name on the list pays out nearly every free cash dollar, and another may be priced too high.

headlines.title: ADP Increases Cash Dividend; Marks 52nd Consecutive Year of Dividend Increases
headlines.summary: The board of directors of ADP (Nasdaq: ADP) approved a $0.20 increase in the quarterly cash dividend to an annual rate of $7.60 per share, Maria Black, ADP's President and Chief Executive Officer, announced today. The increased cash dividend marks the 52nd consecutive year in which ADP, a leading global technology company providing human capital management (HCM) solutions, has raised its quarterly dividend.

headlines.title: ADP: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
headlines.summary: Embedded banking partnerships and cross-border compliance capabilities are quietly building structural advantages that could sustain growth for years.

headlines.title: Did Payroll Data Just Shift ADP Stock's Investment Narrative?
headlines.summary: Automatic Data Processing reported first quarter revenue of US$5,490.7 million and net income of US$1,125.2 million, while also signing a partnership that embeds its payroll and HR tools inside PNC Bank's digital platform for small businesses. Alongside these results, ADP's October payroll report showed 86,000 new private sector jobs and faster worker pay growth, highlighting how its employment data and software both sit close to real world labor and cash flow decisions for clients.

headlines.title: Is Automatic Data Processing (ADP) Priced Right for Its Cash Flow?
headlines.summary: Automatic Data Processing has climbed strongly in recent years, and the question now is whether the current share price fairly reflects the cash flows that shareholders may receive over time. With the stock recently closing at US$303.54, investors are asking how much of the story around ADP's payroll and HR platform is already embedded in the valuation. Over the past 5 years, Automatic Data Processing has delivered a share price return of 48.

description: Automatic Data Processing, Inc. provides cloud-based human capital management (HCM) solutions worldwide. It operates in two segments, Employer Services and Professional Employer Organization (PEO). The Employer Services segment offers strategic, cloud-based platforms, and human resources (HR) outsourcing solutions. This segment's offerings include RUN Powered by ADP, a software platform for small business payroll, HR, and compliance; ADP Workforce Now, a HCM solution used across mid-sized and large businesses to manage employees; and ADP Lyric HCM, a solution for HR management, payroll, workforce management, talent, and data analytics. Its PEO Services segment provides HR outsourcing solutions under ADP TotalSource name to businesses through a co-employment model. This segment also provides guidance, user-friendly technology, comprehensive employee benefits, and a risk management, safety, and workers' compensation program. The company was founded in 1949 and is headquartered in Roseland, New Jersey.
